# The C++ layer: `openrac/mod.hpp`

The C++ layer of the mod interface (docs/port/MODS.md, section 11): header-only, C++17, compiled
into the mod and never into the port. Everything here goes through openrac_mod.h's table, which
stays the boundary; no exception crosses it.

The header is laid out as: the includes, the error and log types, game memory, binds and the
input state, the hook machinery (`detail`), the Mod itself, the stack frame, and last the macro
that writes a mod's entry points. Each item says which interface version added it; the layer
itself needs only the table of the interface the mod was built for.

```cpp
#include "openrac/mod.hpp"
#include "openrac/games/rac1.hpp"
```

```cpp
static void load(openrac::Mod& mod) {
    if (mod.game() != "rac1") throw openrac::Error("this mod is for Ratchet & Clank");
    const bool trace = mod.setting<bool>("trace");
    mod.hook<openrac::rac1::Hero_TurnToHeading>(
        [](auto original, int32_t m, float accel, float damping, float limit) {
            original(m, accel, damping, limit);   // the game's own, or a mod's loaded earlier
        });
    mod.on_frame([] { /* once a game tick */ });
}
OPENRAC_MOD_CPP("my-mod", "0.1.0", load)
```

One library is one mod: the layer keeps one openrac::Mod per library, and each hook point's
callable in a static of its own (a load takes a hook point once; a later load of the same
library starts afresh). An exception out of the
load function becomes the mod's refusal (fail() with its message); one out of a hook or a
callback is logged with the mod's id, and a hook then calls its original, so the game goes on
(a hook that threw after calling the original has it called twice: do not throw there).

## `openrac::Error`

What load and the layer throw: its message is the mod's refusal, or the log's line. Since 1.0.

## `openrac::Memory`

Game memory: typed reads and writes at game addresses. Reads and writes copy (any alignment); ref() gives an lvalue where the address is aligned for T. A view: it owns nothing, and the memory it views lasts for the life of the program. Since 1.0.

| Member | |
|---|---|
| `explicit Memory(std::uint8_t* base)` | Views the memory that begins at `base` (openrac_api.memory). |
| `template <class T> T read(gaddr address) const` | Returns the `T` at `address`, copied out; `T` is a plain value (trivially copyable). |
| `template <class T> void write(gaddr address, const T& value) const` | Copies `value` to `address`; `T` is a plain value (trivially copyable). It does not mark anything the game caches: a value the game keeps elsewhere is the mod's to update. |
| `template <class T> T& ref(gaddr address) const` | Returns the `T` at `address` as an lvalue. The address must be aligned for `T`, and the reference must not be kept across a level load (the level's program moves its globals). |
| `void* pointer(gaddr address) const` | Returns the host pointer to `address`. |
| `std::uint8_t* base() const` | Returns the host pointer to game address 0. |

## `openrac::Input`

The keyboard and mouse for the tick about to run (interface 1.2, openrac_input): a view of the port's state, renewed each tick. Cheap to copy; do not keep it past the tick it was read in.

| Member | |
|---|---|
| `explicit Input(const openrac_input* state)` | Views the port's `state` (openrac_api.input()'s result). |
| `const openrac_input& raw() const` | Returns the C state, for what the accessors do not cover. |
| `bool held(int bind) const` | Returns whether a bind (a key's HID usage, OPENRAC_BIND_*) is held now. |
| `bool pressed(int bind) const` | Returns whether a bind went down since the last tick. |
| `float mouse_dx() const` | Return the mouse's motion since the last tick, in the system's pixels (raw while captured). |
| `float mouse_dy() const` |  |
| `float wheel_x() const` | Return the wheel's turn since the last tick, in notches (x > 0 right, y > 0 up). |
| `float wheel_y() const` |  |
| `bool focused() const` | Return whether the game's window has the keyboard, whether the cursor is captured, and whether the port's own overlay has the input now (leave it alone then). |
| `bool captured() const` |  |
| `bool overlay() const` |  |
| `std::uint32_t tick() const` | Returns the tick counter: a new value is a new state. |
| `bool has_pointer() const` | Since 1.3: returns whether the port's state reaches the pointer fields. False on a 1.2 port, whose pointer_x(), pointer_y() and pointer_inside() then give 0, 0 and false. |
| `float pointer_x() const` | Since 1.3: return where the cursor is over the game's picture, 0..1 across and down (pointer_x() * 512, pointer_y() * 416 is the game's 2D pixel), and whether it is over it. |
| `float pointer_y() const` |  |
| `bool pointer_inside() const` |  |

## `openrac::Original`

`template <class R, class... A>`

| Member | |
|---|---|
| `using fn = R (*)(A...)` |  |
| `explicit Original(fn f)` | Wraps the function `f` that the replacement goes on to. |
| `R operator()(A... args) const` | Calls the original with `args`, as the game would have called the hook point. |
| `fn get() const` | Returns the original as a plain function pointer. |

## `openrac::Mod`

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- The mod ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- The mod as the port loaded it: the table, the handle, and what the mod takes of the game. One per library, made by OPENRAC_MOD_CPP at load; the game's thread is the only one that uses it. Not copyable: the port holds pointers into the callbacks it keeps. Since 1.0.

| Member | |
|---|---|
| `Mod(const openrac_api* api, openrac_mod* handle)` | Wraps the port's table and this mod's handle, as openrac_mod_load received them. |
| `const openrac_api& api() const` | Returns the C table, for what the layer does not wrap. |
| `openrac_mod* handle() const` | Returns the port's handle for this mod, the first argument of the table's own functions. |
| `std::string_view game() const` | Return where the mod runs: the game's id ("rac1"), the disc's version ("pal", "ntsc"), the platform ("macos-arm64", ...) and OpenRAC's version. Valid for the life of the program. |
| `std::string_view version() const` |  |
| `std::string_view platform() const` |  |
| `std::string_view openrac_version() const` |  |
| `unsigned api_major() const` | Return the port's interface version: at least what the mod was built for, else it is not loaded. Check api_minor() before using anything newer than the minor the mod was built for. |
| `unsigned api_minor() const` |  |
| `void log(LogLevel level, const std::string& text) const` | Writes `text` to the session's log at `level`, after the mod's id. |
| `void debug(const std::string& text) const` | Write `text` to the log at the level the name says. |
| `void info(const std::string& text) const` |  |
| `void warn(const std::string& text) const` |  |
| `void error(const std::string& text) const` |  |
| `void fail(const std::string& reason) const` | Says why the mod refuses to load, for status.json and the launcher. Only during load; throwing an openrac::Error from load does the same. |
| `template <class T> T setting(const char* key) const` | Returns a setting of the manifest's, as T: bool for "bool"; an integer type for "int"; float or double for "float"; std::string for "choice" and "string". A key the manifest does not declare, or of another type, gives 0, 0.0, false or "". |
| `template <class HookPoint, class F> void hook(F&& callable)` | Takes the hook point (a type of openrac/games/<game>.hpp) for `callable`, called as callable(original, args...). Throws openrac::Error when the port has no such hook point, a different signature, or the mod already took it. Only during load. |
| `template <class HookPoint> typename HookPoint::fn original() const` | Returns what a hook point this mod took goes on to (as the callable's `original`), for calling it from elsewhere in the mod (another hook, a callback); nullptr before the hook is taken. |
| `template <class F> void on_frame(F&& callable)` | Calls `callable()` after each game tick, in load order. Throws openrac::Error when refused. Only during load. |
| `template <class F> void on_pad(F&& callable)` | Calls `callable(port, report, size)` for each pad report, before the game reads it: the callable may change the report's bytes. Throws openrac::Error when refused. Only during load. |
| `template <class Fn> Fn function(const char* name) const` | Returns a game function by its name in this disc's build, as Fn (a function pointer type); nullptr when there is none. required_function throws openrac::Error instead. |
| `template <class Fn> Fn required_function(const char* name) const` |  |
| `template <class Fn> Fn function_at(gaddr address) const` | Returns the function at a code address of the level loaded now, as Fn; nullptr when there is none. |
| `bool has_input() const` | Since 1.2: returns whether the port offers the keyboard and mouse (input(), take_input(), capture_mouse()): a mod built for 1.2 is loaded only by a port that does, so a mod that wants to run on 1.1 checks this first. |
| `Input input() const` | Since 1.2: returns the keyboard and mouse for the tick about to run. |
| `void take_input(std::uint32_t devices)` | Since 1.2: takes the keyboard (OPENRAC_INPUT_KEYBOARD) and or the mouse from the port's own use of them in play: the mod presses pad 0's buttons through on_pad. Throws openrac::Error when refused. Only during load. |
| `void capture_mouse(bool capture) const` | Since 1.2: asks for the cursor captured (hidden, motion relative) or let go. The port may let it go anyway (window not focused, overlay open). Any time. |
| `bool has_views() const` | Since 1.4: returns whether the port offers the graphics context, views and the Vulkan device (graphics(), on_views(), setup_vulkan()): a mod that wants to run on 1.3 checks this first. |
| `const openrac_graphics &graphics() const` | Since 1.4: returns what the port draws with (openrac_graphics); its backend is OPENRAC_GRAPHICS_NONE before the window opens. |
| `void on_views(const openrac_view_source &source)` | Since 1.4: has the port draw the views `source` asks for each frame (openrac_view_source, sdk/docs/views.md). Throws openrac::Error when refused. Only during load. |
| `void setup_vulkan(const openrac_vulkan_setup &setup)` | Since 1.4: has the port make its Vulkan device through `setup` (openrac_vulkan_setup); the manifest says "vulkan_device": true. Throws openrac::Error when refused. Only during load. |
| `Memory memory() const` | Returns a view of game memory. |
| `gaddr relocate(gaddr address) const` | Return a global's address for the code loaded now: the executable's (`relocate`) or level `level`'s program's (`relocate_level`). Ask each time, because a level moves its globals. |
| `gaddr relocate_level(int level, gaddr address) const` |  |
| `int loaded_level() const` | Returns the level whose program is loaded, -1 for none (the executable's). |

## `openrac::StackFrame`

Room on the game's stack for a call that takes the address of a local, given back when it goes. Not copyable; frames nest and must end innermost first, which scopes do. Since 1.0.

| Member | |
|---|---|
| `StackFrame(const Mod& mod, std::uint32_t size)` | Pushes `size` bytes (aligned to 16) on the game's stack through `mod`'s table. |
| `~StackFrame()` | Pops what the constructor pushed. |
| `gaddr address() const` | Returns the game address of the room. |

## Macros

| Macro | |
|---|---|
| `OPENRAC_MOD_CPP(mod_id, mod_version, load_fn)` | Writes the two entry points of a C++ mod: openrac_mod_query (the id and version, as its manifest's) and openrac_mod_load, which calls load_fn(openrac::Mod&). A throw out of load_fn refuses the load with its message. `mod_id` and `mod_version` are string literals. Since 1.0. |
